notes: Budgets for backend/runner/src/terminals/manager.ts: scripts/ratchet/ratchet.test.ts fails when the file grows past one, and a raise goes only as far as the file needs, never leaving headroom. Set from main at a1fbfdaf (2026-10-17).

slack is how far under its budget the file may sit before the budget must come down. A change that removes a little passes and the test prints the number the budget could be lowered to, so everyday product work never edits this file (about a third of main's commits touch manager.ts, and concurrent pull requests would conflict here). Past the slack, as after an extraction, the test fails until the budget is lowered (in a change that touches manager.ts or this file; any other change only prints it, as two changes merged one after the other can leave the file past a budget neither crossed alone), so a large win is locked in. Lowering a slack needs nothing; raising one is written as a raised budget is, with why and where from.

lines counts the file's lines. methods counts every function the Terminals class defines in its body: methods, accessors, the constructor and properties set to a function or arrow expression, read from its syntax tree, so formatting never moves it.

New behaviour goes in a sibling module under backend/runner/src/terminals/, as closes.ts, opens.ts and titles.ts do, with the class calling it. Work that can't is raised in the same pull request, written { "budget": n, "reason": "why", "from": "#PR or commit" }.

lines.reason: Transcript redaction: three Terminals options (transcriptMs, transcriptShutdownMs, redactor) with their Omit entries, the redactor's construction, the restart's save once the earlier screen is shown, and the restore's once its replay ends; the rest is in saving.ts. Transcript sealing: two more options (sealer, transcriptKeyMs) with their Omit entries and construction, and the restore's open before the shell starts, less the re-save once restored, which sealing makes redundant. Inbox turn rows (+3): Bindings and murmur reach Inbox and the redactor, so the redactor is a local shared with Saves, plus the Bindings host's turns entry. Interrupted-turn notice (+2): the restore reads the saved turn flag through restored(), its import and the call; the logic is in terminals/interrupted.ts. Windows resume (+1): the shell's prompt tells the sampler, which on Windows lets go of the agent a fresh shell resumes only a sample later; the logic is in terminals/sampling.ts. Peer reports (+1): TerminalPeers reads each terminal's latest tell and done from Inbox, as the agents listing shows them; the logic is in messaging/peers.ts. Standing done (+9): Inbox changes, delivered messages and the person's prompts republish the terminal's `reported` summary field through Bindings.publishReported; the rule is `standingDone` in messaging/peers.ts, the logic in terminals/binding/facts.ts. Inbox dismiss (+6, +2 methods): the router reaches Inbox only through Terminals, so dismissAsk and clearAsks forward to it; the logic is in messaging/inbox.ts. open_agent model and effort (+9): the models option (its doc, Omit entry, field, default and the Calls host's entry) carries each harness's model list to the open call, as install does; the checks are in terminals/calls.ts and the lookups in harnesses/service.ts. Close asks (+19): the router reaches the agents' asks to close a terminal through two Terminals methods (closeAsks, answerCloseAsk), as requests and answerRequest, with their field, host entry, imports, and release and shutdown calls; the logic is in terminals/closeasks.ts and calls.ts. Lead an existing agent (+6, +1 method): releaseLead is the router's entry to the person's release of a lead, and the Calls host takes the bindings; the logic is in terminals/leads.ts (closeAsks became approvals, in terminals/approvals.ts). Windows lead (+1): the Bindings host's pollMs entry, so a lead ends on Windows only a sample after its agent, as its resume does; the logic is in terminals/binding/facts.ts. Agent feedback (+12): the router reaches the in-memory drafts through a public `feedback` field, which takes its field, construction, the Calls host's entry, and the project-removal and shutdown calls; the logic is in messaging/feedback.ts. Unstarted worker restore (+3): the restore names the task a led worker lost before its agent's first session starts with again, and gives the record that task's doorbell nonce, as a startup command beside the resume's; the logic is in terminals/resumes.ts. Handle order (+3): the handleOrder option with its doc and Omit entry, which tests set to give handle words in list order; the logic is in terminals/handles.ts and names.ts. open_agent without a task, with a lead and a session to resume (+4): the Calls host takes the claims, and the create judges the session an agent asked to resume again and claims it once the shell runs it; the logic is in terminals/resumes.ts and calls.ts. harness-core split (+1): hookShellSlackMs is imported from @novadeck/harness-core/hook-command, where it moved, a second import line; no new code. Messaging split (+1): SendAnswer and AgentsAnswer are imported from messaging/sending.ts, where they moved, a second import line; no new code. Notes held across restarts (+1): Messaging's held option hands the notes a session holds to Reports.held, which keeps them with its AgentReport; the logic is in terminals/told.ts and binding/reports.ts. Prompt receipts (+1): the detail builder passes the terminal's receipts (typing.receipts.view) to agentDetail beside its dialogs; the logic is in terminals/receipts.ts and receipt-match.ts, and agents.prompt's input and result are typing.ts's PromptInput and Prompted. Agent titles (+1): the Calls host takes `retitle`, so a `describe` shows the title its agent gave at once; the logic is in terminals/calls.ts and titles.ts. Cancelled resume (+2): typing before the shell takes its resume ends the agent expected there, in the record and in Messaging, so murmur describes the programs typed instead and agents() no longer lists it as not started; the logic is in terminals/descriptions.ts. Expecting only a resume that starts (+1): the resume registers its agent only when it runs, and the first prompt after a cancelled or empty startup ends the expectation through endExpecting in terminals/resumes.ts, which also tells murmur. MCP tools before a ring (+3): the reports endpoint's tools handler checks the session's token with callerOf and tells Typing that a terminal's MCP session listed Novadeck's tools, which an Antigravity ring waits for; the logic is in terminals/mcp-tools.ts, typing.ts and doorbell-host.ts. The chat seeing the box (+3): the detail builder passes the box as read (typing.boxes.view) beside the receipts, Streams tells a detail opened, and Typing asks whether anyone reads a detail, so no screen is read for nobody; the logic is in terminals/box-state.ts and typing.ts. One input (+10, +1 method): takeBox and putBox, the router's entries to handing words between the agent's box and a client's draft, as prompt is its entry to giving one; the logic is in typing.ts and libraries/tui-input/src/handover.ts. A startup command waits for its scope (+1): the Launcher host takes the scopes, to tell a shell that one is on its way; the logic is in terminals/launching.ts and the shell integration. Live slice (+15): the `agents.slice` entry the router reaches, the Streams host's `slicing`, the drawn call, and their imports; the logic is in terminals/slices.ts and streams.ts. Passing keys to a harness's menus (+5): keys, the router's entry to `agents.keys`; the logic is in typing.ts and the chat. Clearing the box (+5, +1 method): clearBox, the router's entry to emptying the agent's box as the person asked, beside takeBox and putBox; the logic is in typing.ts and libraries/tui-input/src/handover.ts. Idle agents rest (+67): Hibernation's construction with its host entries (what it reads of the manager, and `rested`, which lets the stopped agent's record go at once and rests its terminal), the settle wait in create, the `hibernating` gates in live, write, attach, announce, prompted and exited, and the attach time the sweep reads; the logic is in terminals/hibernation.ts. Seeing a queued turn (+5): Messaging's stopped option hands each Stop that ends a turn to typing.watchQueue, and the change listener calls it too; the logic is in terminals/typing.ts and messaging/deliveries.ts. Busy shells (+10, +1 method): busyShells, the router's entry to `terminals.busy`, its stopping check, and the shared reader field that lets overlapping calls share one read of the system; the logic is busyTerminals and busyReader in terminals/sampling.ts. Shell-mode commands (+10 over main's 1852): the ShellCommands field with its host entries and import, and its calls from keyed (an Enter), announce (a turn that ended), prompted (the agent left), exited and shutdown; the logic is in terminals/shell-commands.ts.
